item.title: A Time You Had to Adapt
item.prompt_text: Tell the story of a time when you had to adapt to something new, such as a new country, school, job or way of living. Describe the situation, what was difficult, how you dealt with it, and what you learned from the experience.
item.target_grammar: narrative tenses: past simple, past continuous, past perfect; used to
item.fluency_objective: Build the story with time phrases like 'at first', 'after a few weeks' and 'by the end'.
item.pronunciation_objective: Vary your speed and tone: slow down at the most difficult moment of the story to create interest.
item.model_answer: A couple of years ago, I got a six-month internship at a software company in Germany. I'd never lived abroad before, so it was a huge change. At first, almost everything was difficult. I'd studied some German at university, but people spoke much faster than I expected, and I felt embarrassed every time I had to ask them to repeat something. I also really missed my family, especially at weekends, when the city was quiet and I was on my own. The turning point came after about a month. A colleague noticed I was eating lunch alone and invited me to join a group that went running every Saturday. I said yes, even though I was nervous, and slowly I started to make friends. I also decided to speak German in shops, even when I made mistakes, and it took me a while, but I got used to it. Looking back, I learned that adapting isn't about waiting until you feel comfortable. It's about doing small uncomfortable things until they become normal.
